answer: A farm therefore faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Policies are written in vault, settled in thread, and prism lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 44% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. The attacker spends 144 dollars and 14 days per identity before it can vote at all. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
